answer: Stake-weighted reputation with decay works well: each agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, and its trust score grows only from completed work verified by independent peers. If an agent misbehaves, the deposit is slashed and the penalty echoes across its linked identities, so a bad actor cannot simply reappear under a new name. Honest behavior creates a ripple of endorsements that compounds over time, while a raven — a lone malicious identity with no history — starts at zero trust and must earn its way up, making a thousand fake identities far more expensive than one real one.
